one_liner: Shortest round-trip double/float-to-decimal conversion, faster than std::to_chars.
what_it_does: Dragonbox computes the shortest, correctly-rounded, round-trip decimal significand and exponent for a finite nonzero IEEE-754 float/double (jkj::dragonbox::to_decimal), the same job std::to_chars does. A separate layer (dragonbox_to_chars.h + one .cpp) turns that pair into a scientific-notation char buffer via to_chars/to_chars_n. The API is its own namespace with a policy-template surface, not signature-compatible with std::to_chars.
how_it_is_fast: Based on Schubfach (a continuous pigeonhole-principle argument), itself inspired by Grisu/Grisu-Exact. It picks the shortest correctly-rounded decimal digits directly from a precomputed power-of-10 cache table plus magic-number/branchless integer arithmetic, avoiding the big-integer or iterative digit-adjustment loops older dtoa algorithms use. A full cache table (9904 bytes for double) trades static data for speed; a compact table (584 bytes) is ~20% slower.
when_to_use: Hot-path double/float-to-string conversion where scientific-notation output is acceptable and every ns matters
Already depending on {fmt} indirectly and want the same algorithm standalone/header-only without the rest of fmt
x86-64 target with a C++17-capable toolchain (C++20 unlocks constexpr everywhere)
Want to tune static-data footprint via the full-vs-compact cache policy
Need output strictly faster than libc++/libstdc++ std::to_chars on the same double-conversion workload
when_not_to_use: Need std::to_chars-compatible signature/namespace as a true drop-in replacement
Need %f-style fixed-point output directly — Dragonbox only emits scientific notation (0.1 -> 1E-1); you write the reformatting
Targeting ARM or other non-x86 architectures — maintainer-acknowledged correctness bugs in intrinsic fallback/detection are open and unresolved (issue #11, filed 2024)
Require an actual C++11 toolchain — README claims C++11 but the shipped CMakeLists.txt requires cxx_std_17; a C++11 port was requested in 2023 and never delivered (issue #8)
Low-volume/non-hot-path formatting where the ~22ns/call saved over std::to_chars doesn't justify vendoring three files and a template-heavy API

integration.form: header-only (core dragonbox.h); to_chars string-generation layer adds dragonbox_to_chars.h + one .cpp
integration.dependencies: none (C++ standard library only; Ryu/Schubfach/Grisu-Exact in the repo are benchmark-only subprojects, not runtime deps)
integration.min_toolchain: CMakeLists.txt requires cxx_std_17 for both targets; README's 'C++11 or higher' claim is not what the build actually enforces (see issue #8). Full constexpr support needs C++20.
integration.platforms: x86-64 (benchmarked/used in production via fmt); ARM and other architectures have open, maintainer-acknowledged correctness bugs in intrinsic fallback/detection (issue #11, opened 2024, still open) — not documented as safe there
integration.thread_safety: not documented explicitly; grep of dragonbox.h found no mutable static or thread_local state, only constexpr statics over immutable cache tables, so the functions are stateless and inherently thread-safe by construction
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — different namespace/function names than std::to_chars, output is scientific-notation only, and the 5-kind policy-template system changes the call shape further

gotchas: Output is always scientific notation (e.g. 0.1 -> 1E-1), never %f-style; callers add their own formatting for printf-like output
README says C++11 but the CMakeLists.txt pins cxx_std_17 for both the dragonbox and dragonbox_to_chars CMake targets
ARM/non-x86 support has open, maintainer-confirmed correctness bugs in intrinsic fallback detection (issue #11, unresolved since 2024)
Policy-template API (sign, trailing-zero, decimal-to-binary rounding, binary-to-decimal rounding, cache) can cause binary bloat if many policy combinations get instantiated
pick_this_over_siblings_when: On the same fmtlib/dtoa-benchmark table, Dragonbox (28.95ns) beats both catalogued siblings Ryu (46.07ns) and {fmt} (36.84ns) and is the only one of the three verified directly against std::to_chars rather than just sprintf; pick it over them when raw to_chars-class conversion speed is the goal and the policy-template API/scientific-notation-only output are acceptable, and pick {fmt} instead when you also want its broader formatting API (fmt already uses Dragonbox internally). fast_float solves the reverse problem (string-to-double parsing), so it's complementary, not a substitute.
verified_claims_summary: On the independent fmtlib/dtoa-benchmark suite (Apple M1 Pro, Apple clang 21.0.0, Release build via libc++), Dragonbox's to_chars_n with the full cache table converts a double to its shortest round-trip decimal string in a mean 28.95ns vs 51.35ns for libc++'s std::to_chars (1.77x) and 744.72ns for sprintf (25.72x), over a mixed 1.7M-value pool spanning 1-17 significant digits.
status_note: Stale by commit cadence (last commit 2025-09-12, ~1 year old) but not abandoned — issues still receive maintainer replies through 2026; dual Apache-2.0-with-LLVM-exception/BSL-1.0 licensing and a 3-file footprint for the to_chars path make it easy to vendor despite the slow pace.
